newsitem.title: FRANCE: French roaster Cafes Excella to raise retail price.
newsitem.headline: French roaster Cafes Excella to raise retail price.

text.p: French Cafes Excella SA, a distributor brand that has a five percent market share, said on Friday that it planned to further raise retail prices in June.

This meant that the average price of one kg of arabica coffee would increase by five to six francs and that of one kg of robusta by between two and three francs as of June 1, marketing director Jean-Jacques Dothee told Reuters.
The group already raised its retail prices by some 33 percent for arabicas and by six percent for robustas during the first four months of 1997.
Earlier Douwe Egberts France said it had raised retail prices by 1.50 francs per 250 grams of arabica coffee and by 65 centimes for each pack of robusta coffee, with immediate effect.
Dothee said roasters operating on tight stocks were very vulnerable to volatile prices, which he said did not reflect market fundamentals.
"There is no risk of a coffee shortage. We are being held hostage by a speculative game which does not reflect the reality," he said.
On Thursday speculative buying in the face of tight supplies in Latin America and low stocks in consumer countries drove New York coffee futures to their highest levels in 20 years.
Dothee also said that he expected the prices of some washed Latin American arabicas to remain high until the end of the year.
But the prices of other coffees might ease in autumn, provided there was no frost in Brazil, he said.
Dothee also warned that high prices might scare away consumers, notably young people.

In 1994 and 1995 French roasters passed on the cost to consumers of higher world futures, and consumption fell by seven percent he said. Consumption rebounded by three percent in 1996 when retail prices went down, he said.
"If coffee prices remain too high, we are going to lose customers," he said.
He said young people in particular were likely to switch to soft drinks and to cheaper coffee brands.
